value.rationale: Maintaining a genuinely multipartite entangled resource against isotropic local decoherence is a natural model-design constraint. The exact all-size feasibility boundary and its extensive cost with universal constant correction give a sharp quantitative tradeoff: simply increasing system size at fixed reset rate necessarily destroys stationary genuine multipartite entanglement. This differs qualitatively from known amplitude-damping protocols. An exact maintenance-rate classification is mathematically substantive even without a broader quantum-computing performance theorem; ideal entangled restoration costs are clearly disclosed.
